timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The main part of an identity is the language.
As a teenager when I grew up in France, I had this identity crisis.
I felt the need to choose between being French or being Tunisian.
A week's script, and there would be a calligraphy,
made me reconnect between those two identities.
Today I want to use this as a tool to create the same connection between other culture
and other people in other generations.
And there are big scripts also as some shapes that other alphabet doesn't have.
And it gives you so much opportunity or possibility to create with no limit.
The quote actually is what Rally Gibran wrote on his grave.
And it says, I'm alive like you.
Standing beside you, close your eyes and you will see maybe in front of you.

youtube_description: eL Seed is a French-Tunisian artist who creates large-scale ‘calligraffiti’ murals across the world. Growing up in Paris, he only learnt to write in Arabic script as an adult. Upon learning the art of Arabic calligraphy he discovered that it helped him reconcile the two halves of his Tunisian and French identity. Here he tells us how he uses the beauty of writing to create connections between different cultures. #MakingYourMark
youtube_title: eL Seed: How writing creates connections between different cultures
